title: Living in Seoul 2026: The Complete Expat Guide
description: Thinking about moving to Seoul? This guide covers everything: visas, neighborhoods, cost of living, healthcare, banking, and settling in.
content:
Seoul consistently ranks among the world's most liveable cities — clean, safe, connected, and culturally rich. An estimated 150,000 non-Korean expats call Seoul home. Here's what moving here actually looks like in 2026.

Visa Options for Long-Term Stay

  • E-2 (English Teaching) — Most common route for native English speakers. Requires degree and TEFL/CELTA for most employers.
  • D-8 (Corporate Investment) — For those establishing businesses with ₩100M+ investment
  • F-2 (Residential) — For those with qualifying points (language, education, income)
  • D-10 (Job Seeker) — New visa for skilled workers job-hunting in Korea
  • Digital Nomad Visa — Launched 2023, for remote workers earning from foreign companies

Cost of Living (Monthly Estimates)

One-bedroom apartment (Mapo)₩800,000-1,200,000
Utilities (all)₩150,000-250,000
Groceries₩400,000-600,000
Eating out (daily lunch)₩8,000-12,000
Monthly transit pass₩55,000

Best Neighborhoods for Expats

  • Itaewon/Hannam-dong — Most international, best English-language services
  • Mapo-gu (Yeonnam, Hongdae) — Creative community, younger expats, excellent cafes
  • Gangnam (Seocho, Banpo) — Families, international schools, premium amenities
  • Seongdong-gu (Seongsu, Haengdang) — Rising area, creative workers, emerging community
💡 Healthcare Tip: Korea's National Health Insurance (NHI) covers all legal residents within 6 months of arrival. Contributions are income-based (~3-4% of salary for employees). Korean healthcare quality is exceptionally high.
